# 3D observatory and simulator interface

The main simulation and mapping/communication observatory share the existing
cream, sage and forest palette. The legacy ROS dashboard is replaced by the
unified observatory at `/?mode=ros`; browser missions open at
`/?mode=observatory` without replacing their running engine or PPO bridge.

## Implemented

- Three.js occupancy geometry, rover/drone models, raised measured walls,
  trajectories, goals and transport-driven packet arcs.
- Isometric/top-down camera, orbit/pan/zoom, reset, visualization freeze and
  individual packet/path/frontier layer controls.
- Selected-agent inspection and private-map identity; missing data stays
  unavailable and unobserved space remains blank.
- Collapsible message stream, delivery/drop filters and JSON export.
- ROS connection dialog, stale/disconnected states and actual isolation service
  controls whose state follows ROS network telemetry.
- Graphics failure/context-loss recovery while mission and message controls
  remain accessible.
- Compact main-world HUD, grouped display controls, responsive playback dock,
  fleet/settings/help drawers and clean-view toggle.
- Public English audio fieldbook link in the simulation header.

## Verification evidence

`artifacts/observatory_redesign/frontend_tests.txt` records the 146 frontend
tests. Production TypeScript/Vite build passes. Browser interaction evidence,
including screenshots, is in `artifacts/observatory_redesign/validation.json`
and `world_validation.json`.

ROS and PPO browser fixtures validate interface contracts and session continuity.
They do not establish live Linux SLAM, Gazebo motion or actor inference. The
browser mission tests use actual simulator state and transport logs. The ROS
fixture controls its wall clock so GPU rendering delays cannot accidentally age
its synthetic messages; it explicitly advances time to verify stale controls.

## Audiobook deployment

The separate static fieldbook is deployed at https://swarmsar.vercel.app using
the authenticated Vercel project `swarmsar`. Public browser checks verified
page navigation, recorded English narration, byte-range seeking, search,
mobile bounds, PDF and chaptered M4B downloads. Evidence is in
`artifacts/audiobook_vercel/validation.json`.

The fieldbook is the documented source edition from 30 October 2026; its
historical source atlas is not automatically regenerated by simulator edits.
